topics.topic: Exact stable sandbox implementation module name and collision handling
questions: What exact, deterministic module name is assigned to an implementation, and how are collisions with standard-library or runner modules prevented or handled?
What exact, stable module name must the loader assign to an implementation, and how are collisions with modules already present in `sys.modules` handled?

quotes: It is loaded as a standard import loads a module: entered in `sys.modules` under its own name before its body runs, so code that looks its own module up by name (`dataclasses` under postponed annotations, `typing.get_type_hints`) behaves as it does under an import.
6. The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
12. A module using `dataclasses` under `from __future__ import annotations`, and one reading its own entry in `sys.modules`, load and conclude `passed`.
judgement.divergence: One implementation assigns a fixed generic module name, while another assigns an implementation-derived name; an agent inspecting the TrialExecution sees different output from code returning `__name__`, and collision handling can likewise change whether loading succeeds.
judgement.why: The new rule requires insertion under the module's own name but leaves the observable name and collision policy to the implementer.

topics.topic: Ordering and pagination of tools/list catalogue entries
questions: Does A16 rule 6 apply to `tools/list`; if not, in what order and in how many responses are catalogue entries returned?

quotes: `tools/list` answers one tool per catalogue operation, in catalogue order, without pagination, its `inputSchema` derived from the operation's request model by a closed rule (State 7); `tools/call` runs the operation.

answer_request: [BEHAVIOR] The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, parsed only after the depth check, which follows the size and token checks. A JSON object whose jsonrpc is "2.0" with a string method and an id is a request; one with a method and no id is a notification and one with no method a response: both are answered with empty bytes and change nothing. A request's method decides: initialize answers the result {protocolVersion: the imported MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant, capabilities: {tools: {listChanged: false}}, serverInfo: {name: the imported MCP_SERVER_NAME constant, version: the imported MCP_SERVER_VERSION constant}} whatever version its params ask, and keeps no state; ping answers an empty result object; tools/list answers {tools: [...]} as below, ignoring any cursor; tools/call names the catalogue operation in params.name and carries its request in params.arguments, which then pass the remaining checks of the first note.
judgement.why: Later text requires one unpaginated response in catalogue order and explicitly ignores any cursor.

topics.topic: Required lifetime of the implementation entry in sys.modules
questions: Must the implementation remain at `sys.modules[__name__]` through the call to `run`, or may the runner remove it after module initialization?

quotes: It is loaded as a standard import loads a module: entered in `sys.modules` under its own name before its body runs, so code that looks its own module up by name (`dataclasses` under postponed annotations, `typing.get_type_hints`) behaves as it does under an import.
12. A module using `dataclasses` under `from __future__ import annotations`, and one reading its own entry in `sys.modules`, load and conclude `passed`.
judgement.divergence: One runner keeps the implementation at `sys.modules[__name__]` while `run` executes, whereas another removes it after module initialization; the caller sees `true` versus `false` or a crash from code inspecting that entry.
judgement.why: The rule fixes insertion before the module body but does not say whether the entry persists through the subsequent call to `run`.
